How a Businessman With Legal Troubles Bought a Huge Chunk of Trump’s Cryptocurrency
Last year, an unknown company made a stunning announcement — it had bought $100 million in digital tokens from President Trump’s crypto business. We decided to explore the man behind it.
Guren “Bobby” Zhou had failed as a retail store owner in Britain and started over as a crypto entrepreneur. I found a string of his announcements claiming major financial backers.
But when I contacted those supposed partners — companies owned by the Chinese government and the Abu Dhabi royal family, and British celebrities — they denied giving him money.
Zhou’s associates told me that his first crypto company had raised a few million dollars and failed. He moved to Abu Dhabi while under investigation in Britain for money laundering.
His new companies soon bought the Trump tokens. Zhou’s background raises questions about how thoroughly the Trumps’ company, World Liberty Financial, vetted him before accepting his money.
